WHAT MAKES US EPIC?

 At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

 Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

 PROGRAMMING - EPIC RESEARCH

 What We Do 

 Epic Research conducts state-of-the-art research in machine learning, AI, character animation, and digital humans. We work with leading universities and product teams to bring new research into games like Fortnite, Unreal Engine, MetaHuman, and the tools creators use every day.

 MACHINE LEARNING RESEARCH INTERNSHIP AT EPIC GAMES

 What You'll Do 

 Epic Games is looking for current PhD students and recent PhD graduates (within 12 months of graduation) for paid research internships, working on state-of-the-art machine learning across our ecosystem. Epic makes Unreal Engine, which powers creative work across many industries, alongside some of the world's most popular games, including Fortnite and Rocket League. Through these products, ML research at Epic reaches millions of creators and players every day. AI is reshaping the games industry, and Epic Research - led by Lucia Specia and Michael Black - is at the center of that shift. We're looking for talented interns who want to be part of it.

 In this role, you will 

 Work with our team of research scientists and programmers at the intersection of vision, language, speech processing, embodied agents, and game development to create state-of-the-art machine learning models in a range of areas - research topics of interest include:

• AI-backed interactive characters : LLMs for conversational characters, memory systems, automated evals, animation, etc. 

• Game agents : vision-language-action, game-state agents, etc. 

• 3D human and object tracking 

• Reinforcement learning for embodied behavior 

• Speech systems and conversational agents 

• World building and game logic generation : video models, 2D->3D scene building, etc. 

• AI-assisted game development , e.g. the next generation of Epic Developer Assistant for UE and UEFN 

• Embodied and physical intelligence including human-object interaction 

• Multi-modal diffusion models 

• Player safety : AI-alignment, content moderation, etc. 

• Improved user experience : personalised game recommendation, game representation, spam detection, etc. 

• Content localization : (multimodal) translation, quality assurance, etc. 

• Model distillation for realtime performance 
 
 What we're looking for 

• An ongoing or recently completed (within the last 12 months) PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, AI or a related field 

• A record of publication in top conferences/journals 

• Experience implementing deep learning algorithms for problems in computer vision, natural language processing, or speech/audio processing 

• Hands-on knowledge of state-of-the-art ML methods, such as Transformers, diffusion models, and reinforcement learning 

• Experience with post-training foundation models, including SFT, preference training, and reinforcement learning 

• Excellent AI coding and experimental programming skills 

• Desirable: game development experience in either C++ or C# 
 
 Internship Details 

• Duration : 5-12 months initially (depending on your location), with flexible start-dates throughout 2026/2027 

• Hours : full-time (40 hours/week) or part-time (20 hours/week) 

• Location: Select regions within North America and Europe 

• Employment Authorization: You must hold an existing right to work in your given location for the full duration of the internship - visa sponsorship or support is unavailable for this role 

• Publishing : Research by Epic interns is regularly published in top-tier conferences 
 
 This internship has a flexible start date in 2026/2027. Recruitment will be ongoing until teams find an ideal match. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the posting location for the duration of the internship. For more information about Epic’s Early Career Program, visit epicgames.com/earlycareers . Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation.

About the role:

Join our engineering team for a 16-week paid internship (JAN - APRIL) where you'll work alongside world-class engineers, designers, and product managers to build the future of software creation. You'll contribute to real features that impact millions of developers worldwide, from our AI-powered development environment to the infrastructure that makes lightning-fast collaboration possible.

 Responsibilities
 The Data-AML-Engine Orchestration team builds large-scale machine learning infrastructure that powers online model serving across ByteDance products, including TikTok. We develop the orchestration, scheduling, and resource management systems that connect heterogeneous compute infrastructure with production ML workloads.
You will work on systems that directly affect GPU utilization, serving latency and availability, infrastructure reliability, and MLE productivity. Depending on your background and interests, you may focus on one or more of the following areas.

We are looking for talented individuals to join us for an internship. Our internship program offers students hands-on experience, industry exposure, and opportunities to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges while building a strong foundation for personal and professional growth.
Interns will gain practical experience, explore potential career paths, and participate in social events, learning programs, and development workshops alongside industry professionals.
Candidates may apply to a maximum of two positions across Our Company and its affiliates globally. Applications will be considered in the order they are submitted.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early. Please clearly state your availability in your resume, including your start and end dates.

Responsibilities:
- Design and build foundational orchestration capabilities for machine learning platforms, including Kubernetes Operators, container runtimes, and lifecycle management for jobs, services, and stateful workloads.
- Build multi-tenant resource and quota systems that support priorities, preemption, fair sharing, elasticity, and cross-cluster scheduling. Improve GPU utilization and cost efficiency through resource pooling and FinOps.
- Build lifecycle orchestration for online model serving, including model and image distribution, deployment, upgrades, rollback, autoscaling, multi-cluster operation, and disaster recovery.
- Build serving orchestration and traffic management capabilities for disaggregated serving clusters, including topology-aware scheduling, KV Cache affinity, intelligent request routing, and QoS/SLA management.

 Qualifications
 Minimum Qualifications:
- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related technical field.
- Proficiency in at least one of Go, C++, or Python, with a solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.
- Familiarity with Linux and a foundational understanding of operating systems, computer networks, concurrent programming, and distributed systems.
- Strong hands-on and exploratory abilities, with a willingness to investigate systems through source code, metrics, logs, profiling, and experiments.
- A systematic and quantitative approach to problem solving, with the ability to define measurements, test hypotheses, and validate system improvements.
- Demonstrated ownership and collaboration through coursework, research, internships, open-source contributions, or other engineering projects.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience with Kubernetes, container runtimes, resource scheduling, quota management, multi-tenant systems, or FinOps.
- Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects such as Kubernetes, Volcano, Koordinator, or OpenKruise.
- Experience with model serving systems such as vLLM, SGLang, Triton, KServe, or Ray Serve, or an understanding of KV Cache, Continuous Batching, Prefill/Decode disaggregation, or model parallelism.
- Experience with online services, gateways, traffic management, autoscaling, performance optimization, or highly available distributed systems.
- Experience with GPU/NPU programming, heterogeneous resource scheduling, model distribution, or inference performance analysis.

PHARMACOGENOMICS DATA SCIENCE & GENOMIC PREDICTION INTERN Location: Kalamazoo, MI
 Internship Summary: Zoetis Precision Animal Health - Veterinary Medicine Research & Development (PAH VMRD) is seeking a summer intern to support a pharmacogenomic project, a novel platform exploring how genetic variation influences treatment response in livestock. The intern will work directly with the project team lead to mine and integrate dairy cattle health and treatment datasets, define treatment response phenotypes for mastitis, and develop proof-of-concept genomic prediction models contributing to a first-of-its-kind pharmacogenomic decision support system for animal health.
 Internship Job Duties: 
 • Extract, clean, and integrate clinical treatment records and health event data from dairy herd management systems (e.g., Dairy Comp 305) and link with existing genotype data to build analysis-ready datasets.
 • Define and construct treatment response phenotypes for mastitis/ bovine respiratory disease, including clinical cure, bacteriological cure, relapse, recurrence.
 • Evaluate existing SNP panel and sequence data to identify DNA markers and candidate genomic regions with potential predictive value for mastitis/bovine respiratory disease treatment outcomes.
 • Develop and test proof-of-concept genomic prediction models (e.g., GBLUP, BayesR, or machine learning approaches) for treatment response traits, including preliminary accuracy and heritability estimates.
 Internship Qualifications: 
 • Currently enrolled in a Master's or PhD program in Animal Science, Quantitative Genetics, Animal Breeding & Genomics, Bioinformatics, or a closely related field.
 • Experience with genomic data analysis, including GWAS, genomic prediction, and/or variance component estimation using mixed models.
 • Proficiency in at least one programming or statistical environment (R, Python, SAS, or equivalent) for large-scale data manipulation and analysis.
 • Familiarity with livestock health data, dairy herd management systems, or genomic selection concepts is strongly preferred.
 • Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and present results to a cross-functional team.

Job Description 
 Work Arrangement:   
 Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week. 

 Location:   
 Sunnyvale, CA 

 About the Team 
 The Data Scaling team builds the data, machine learning, and infrastructure foundations that enable Embodied AI models to improve with scale. We work across data collection, curation, mining, labeling, dataset quality, model inputs, distributed training, experiment workflows, and the systems that help researchers and engineers develop, evaluate, and deploy models more efficiently.

 Our work supports large-scale autonomous driving models and the broader Embodied AI flywheel. We combine machine learning, data engineering, distributed systems, and software engineering to make high-quality, product-aligned driving data available for perception, planning, trajectory generation, and other autonomy capabilities.

 About the Role 
 As an Embodied AI Data Scaling Intern, you will work on a well-scoped project that improves the scale, quality, efficiency, or reliability of data and model development for autonomous driving. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to build data pipelines, analyze large datasets, improve training workflows, or develop infrastructure that increases the number and quality of experiments the team can run.

 Potential focus areas include:
 
• Data Curation and Quality: Build methods to select, filter, balance, and validate large driving datasets aligned with product and modeling needs. 
• Data Mining and Scenario Discovery: Identify valuable, rare, or challenging driving situations and develop tools to improve coverage of long-tail scenarios. 
• Dataset and Labeling Pipelines: Improve automated labeling, data transformation, feature generation, and dataset release workflows. 
• Distributed Training and Model Scaling: Optimize the systems, input pipelines, and compute workflows used to train large models on large datasets. 
• ML Experimentation and Flywheel Infrastructure: Build tools that help teams develop, train, evaluate, debug, and deploy models more quickly and reliably. 
 What You’ll Do 
 
• Develop data pipelines and tooling for large-scale, multimodal autonomous driving datasets. 
• Analyze data quality, coverage, distribution, and performance impact using quantitative methods. 
• Prototype and evaluate approaches for data mining, curation, labeling, sampling, or scenario discovery. 
• Improve training throughput, data loading, experiment reproducibility, or resource utilization in distributed computing environments. 
• Collaborate with machine learning researchers, data engineers, infrastructure engineers, and autonomy teams. 
• Build visualizations, metrics, dashboards, and evaluation workflows to communicate data and model behavior. 
• Contribute to production-quality software through design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation. 
• Present technical findings and document experiments, results, and recommendations. 
 Required Qualifications 
 
• Currently enrolled in or pursuing a Master’s or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
• Demonstrated experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or professional work in machine learning, data engineering, distributed systems, or a related area. 
• Strong programming skills in Python. 
• Experience working with data processing, databases, machine learning pipelines, or large-scale datasets. 
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use quantitative analysis to guide decisions. 
• Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment. 
• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills. 
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 
• Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or another machine learning framework. 
• Experience with distributed training, parallel computing, high-performance computing, cloud infrastructure, or GPU-based workflows. 
• Familiarity with multimodal sensor data, autonomous vehicles, robotics, computer vision, or large-scale time-series data. 
• Experience with SQL, data warehouses, workflow orchestration, data quality systems, or distributed data-processing frameworks. 
• Familiarity with foundation models, self-supervised learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, or deep learning. 
• Experience with C++ or another systems programming language. 
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 
• Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship. 
 Compensation:  
 
• The monthly salary range for this role is $11,800 – $14,600 per month   
• GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program.  
 What You’ll Get from Us 
 
• Paid U.S. GM holidays. 
• GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program. 
• Potential for growth within GM based on performance and business needs. 
• Intern events and opportunities to network with company leaders and peers. 
• Mentorship and hands-on experience with the data and ML foundations behind autonomy

Job Description 
 Work Arrangement:   
 Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week. 

 Location:   
 Sunnyvale, CA 

 About the Team 
 The State Estimation, Alignment, and Mapping (SEAM) team develops the sensing and spatial understanding capabilities that help autonomous vehicles know where they are, interpret their surroundings, and maintain reliable operation over time. The team works on sensor fusion, state estimation, real-time localization, static and dynamic sensor calibration, next-generation mapping, and capabilities that support primary and fallback driving systems.

 SEAM combines robotics, computer vision, estimation theory, machine learning, geometry, and production software engineering. Our work supports both onboard, real-time autonomy and offboard, high-fidelity map and data-generation workflows.

 About the Role 
 As a SEAM Intern, you will work on a well-scoped research or engineering project related to sensing, estimation, localization, mapping, or autonomy reliability. You will collaborate with experienced engineers and researchers to design algorithms, implement software, evaluate system performance, and understand how sensing capabilities operate in real-world autonomous driving systems.

 Potential focus areas include:
 
• State Estimation and Sensor Fusion: Combine information from multiple sensors and vehicle signals to estimate position, orientation, motion, and other states robustly. 
• Sensor Alignment and Calibration: Develop methods for static and dynamic calibration, sensor registration, and maintaining alignment as vehicle and environmental conditions change. 
• Localization: Improve real-time localization and map-based positioning across diverse driving environments. 
• Next-Generation Mapping: Build or evaluate high-fidelity, large-scale maps that provide useful spatial context beyond the immediate sensor range. 
• Fallback and Secondary Capabilities: Develop reliable estimation, localization, or mapping functions that support safe operation when nominal system capabilities are unavailable or degraded. 
 What You’ll Do 
 
• Develop, prototype, and evaluate algorithms for sensor fusion, state estimation, localization, calibration, mapping, or related autonomy capabilities. 
• Work with camera, lidar, radar, inertial, vehicle, map, and other multimodal data sources. 
• Implement software and tools for data processing, visualization, offline analysis, simulation, and system evaluation. 
• Analyze accuracy, robustness, latency, and failure modes across diverse operating conditions. 
• Apply software engineering best practices, including design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation. 
• Collaborate with perception, planning, controls, robotics, systems engineering, and vehicle-program partners. 
• Communicate technical findings and contribute to design discussions and project documentation. 
 Required Qualifications 
 
• Currently enrolled in or pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field. 
• Demonstrated experience through coursework, research, academic projects, or professional work in robotics, state estimation, sensor fusion, computer vision, localization, mapping, controls, or a related area. 
• Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python. 
• Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, geometry, optimization, or estimation methods. 
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 
• Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional, team-oriented environment. 
• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills. 
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship period. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 
• Experience with Kalman filtering, factor graphs, SLAM, visual-inertial odometry, bundle adjustment, point clouds, geometric computer vision, or multi-sensor calibration. 
• Familiarity with autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, robotics, ROS, or safety-critical systems. 
• Experience with large-scale sensor or map datasets, simulation, data association, or offline evaluation. 
• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX. 
• Familiarity with real-time systems, distributed systems, high-performance computing, or production software development 
• Intent to return to a degree program after completion of the internship or co-op. 
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 
 Compensation:  
 
• The monthly salary range for this role is $14,600 per month   
• GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program.  
 What You’ll Get from Us 
 
• Paid U.S. GM holidays. 
• GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program. 
• Potential for growth within GM based on performance and business needs. 
• Intern events and opportunities to network with company leaders and peers. 
• Mentorship and hands-on experience with the data and ML foundations behind autonomy

 Location:   
 Sunnyvale, CA 
 Seattle, WA

 About the Team 
 The Onboard Autonomy team develops the real-time intelligence that enables autonomous vehicles to perceive their surroundings, plan safe and comfortable behavior, and operate reliably on the vehicle. Our work spans sensor fusion, structured perception, trajectory generation, ML planning, local planning, controls, guardrails, evaluation, and vehicle integration.

 We combine machine learning, robotics, optimization, and software engineering to build production-oriented autonomy systems that operate in real time and handle challenging driving scenarios.

 About the Role 
 As an Onboard Autonomy Intern, you will contribute to a focused research or engineering project within the onboard driving stack. You will work with experienced researchers and engineers to prototype, evaluate, and improve algorithms or software using vehicle data, simulation, or production-oriented environments.

 Potential focus areas include:
 
• Sensor Encoders and Fusion: Convert camera, lidar, radar, and other sensor inputs into useful representations for autonomy. 
• Structured Perception: Improve object tracking, online maps, scene understanding, and long-tail scenario handling. 
• ML Planning and Trajectory Generation: Predict behavior, generate trajectories, and select safe driving actions. 
• Local Planning and Controls: Balance collision avoidance, traffic rules, vehicle dynamics, kinematic feasibility, and passenger comfort. 
• Guardrails and Integration: Validate and integrate autonomy components across vehicle platforms to support safe, reliable operation. 
 What You’ll Do 
 
• Prototype and evaluate algorithms for perception, prediction, planning, trajectory generation, controls, or integration. 
• Work with real-world driving data and simulation to measure performance and investigate failures. 
• Build data-processing, visualization, testing, and evaluation tools. 
• Contribute to production-quality software through design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation. 
• Analyze results, improve system performance, collaborate across disciplines, and present technical findings. 
 Required Qualifications 
 
• Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Controls, Machine Learning, or a related STEM field. 
• Experience through coursework, research, projects, or professional work in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, controls, optimization, or autonomous systems. 
• Strong Python skills and experience with C++ or another systems programming language. 
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. 
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship. 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 
• Experience with autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, or ROS. 
• Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, deep learning, transformers, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or trajectory prediction. 
• Background in vehicle dynamics, feedback control, trajectory optimization, motion planning, safety-critical software, simulation, closed-loop evaluation, sensor data, large-scale datasets, or distributed computing. 
• Intent to return to a degree program after the internship or co-op. 
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028 
 Compensation:  
 
• The monthly salary range for this role is $14,600 per month   
• GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program.  
 What You’ll Get from Us 
 
• Paid U.S. GM holidays. 
• GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program. 
• Potential for growth within GM based on performance and business needs. 
• Intern events and opportunities to network with company leaders and peers. 
• Mentorship and hands-on experience with the data and ML foundations behind autonomy

The Bosch Research and Technology Center North America with offices in Sunnyvale, California, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and Cambridge, Massachusetts is a part of the global Bosch Group (www.bosch.com), a company with over 70 billion euro revenue, 400,000 employees worldwide, a very diverse product portfolio, and a history spanning over 125 years. The Research and Technology Center North America (RTC-NA) is dedicated to providing technologies and system solutions for various Bosch business fields, primarily in the field of artificial intelligence, energy technologies, internet technologies, circuit design, semiconductors and wireless, as well as advanced MEMS design. 
 As a part of the global research, our AI research in Silicon Valley focuses on Foundation Models, Big Data Visual Analytics, Explainable AI (XAI), Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision & Mixed Reality, Cloud Robotics, Data Science, AI System Engineering, Time-series Analysis. We develop scalable, intelligent, and trustworthy AIoT solutions for Bosch products and services in application areas such as automated driving, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, smart manufacturing, enterprise AI, health care, smart home and building solutions. 
 Originating from the AI research in Silicon Valley, our  Foundation Model Powered AI Enablers  group plays a pivotal role in shaping the future of industrial AI experiences for Bosch products and services. By fusing cutting-edge machine learning, data analysis, and interactive visualization technologies, we research and develop scalable and transparent AI & big data analytic solutions (e.g., audio, images, sensor logs) for a range of domains, including Industry 4.0 (I4.0), IoT, autonomous driving, and connected vehicles. Our award-winning team (IEEE VIS best paper & best paper runner-ups) actively collaborates with leading academic and industry groups to advance research ideas and disseminate findings in top AI conferences and journals, such as CVPR, ICCV, ICRA, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, TVCG, SIGGRAPH. 
 We Are Bosch. 
 At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high-quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives.  The Applied Machine Learning Ark team combines system engineering and machine learning to develop and operate Large Language Model (LLM) service platforms that offer businesses Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) solutions, serving both large model providers and downstream users. We have multiple openings for  undergraduate students  to join the Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Summer Institute (CSI) and to work on topics related to power systems resilience and security that align with LLNL’s national security missions. • Provide technical and/or research support to projects in the areas of power systems, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, and other related fields working with scientists, engineers, and technical staff members.

• power systems 
• industrial control systems 
• transmission or distribution system modeling or simulation 
• oil and natural gas systems modeling or simulation 
• distributed energy resources, inverter-based resources, or microgrids 
• alternative energy systems 
• grid planning or operations algorithms, optimization, or analytics

• Attend relevant seminars and training classes (at least one per week). 
• Present work in at least one seminar or poster. 
• Perform other duties as assigned.

Posting Title 
Graduate (10-12 weeks) Intern - AI/ML for Cybersecurity . 
 Location 
CO - Golden . 
 Position Type 
Intern (Fixed Term) . 
 Hours Per Week 
40 . 
 Working at NLR 
NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development. 
 Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.
 
 At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

 Job Description 
 The intern will conduct hands-on research at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, and critical energy infrastructure security. The position focuses on enhancing the reliability, transparency, and operator-readiness of AI-driven cybersecurity tools used to secure power grid substations and physical assets, with a primary focus on explainability and robust uncertainty bounds.

 ·       Explainable AI (XAI): Design and implement XAI methods (e.g., attribution maps, rule extraction, root-cause analyses) to make complex ML models transparent and auditable for control-room operators and system administrators.
 ·       Confidence & Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistical techniques and frameworks (e.g., conformal prediction, Bayesian neural networks, or ensemble methods) to quantify model confidence and measure predictive uncertainty in real-time.
 ·       Grid Dataset Analysis: Analyze cyber-physical power system security datasets (such as 9-Bus system baseline and cyber-physical anomaly runs) to extract feature patterns and validate anomaly detection model behavior.
 ·       Model Safety & Robustness: Explore machine learning safety techniques, including model steering, to ensure grid security models behave predictably under distribution shifts or input corruptions.
 ·       Visualization & Alert Design: Support research into visualization methods and alert design that present explainability and confidence metrics clearly to operators, assisting with alert prioritization.
 ·       Collaboration & Reporting: Partner with cybersecurity researchers and AI development teams to integrate explainability modules, document results, and compile guidelines for deploying reliable AI models.
 . 
 Basic Qualifications 
Minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average.

Undergraduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a bachelor’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Undergraduate: Earned a bachelor’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.

Graduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a master’s degree program from an accredited institution. 
Post Graduate: Earned a master’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.
Graduate + PhD: Completed master’s degree and enrolled as PhD student from an accredited institution. 

Please Note:
• Applicants are responsible for uploading official or unofficial school transcripts, as part of the application process.
• If selected for position, a letter of recommendation will be required as part of the hiring process.
• Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 * Must meet educational requirements prior to employment start date. 
 
 Additional Required Qualifications 
 ·       Education: Currently pursuing or completed a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, AI, Applied Mathematics, or Statistics.
 ·       Programming & ML Frameworks: Strong proficiency in Python; hands-on experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Hugging Face.
 ·       Core Research Competency: Substantial coursework or project experience in Explainable AI (XAI) , machine learning safety, confidence calibration, or statistical uncertainty modeling.
 ·       Generative AI / LLMs: Practical experience working with Large Language Models (LLMs) or Foundation Models or other complex deep neural networks.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 ·       Active research/publications in top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, IEEE S&P, USENIX Security, or ACM CCS) with a focus on XAI, robust ML, or cyber-physical energy systems.
 ·       Experience with specialized explainability libraries (such as Captum, SHAP, or LIME) and uncertainty calibration methods.
 ·       Familiarity with multi-sensor data fusion, power systems modeling, or grid anomaly detection.
 ·       Contributions to open-source software libraries focusing on AI transparency, reliability, or security.
 .

At Rhoda AI, we’re building the next generation of generalist intelligent robots. We own the full robotics stack from high-performance hardware and robot systems to the infrastructure and state-of-the-art foundation world models that control our robots. Our robots are designed to be generalists capable of operating in complex, real-world environments and handling long-tail edge cases, made possible by our cutting edge research and end-to-end system design. We've raised over $450M and are investing aggressively in model research, infrastructure, hardware development, and manufacturing scale-up to make generalist robotics a reality.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer Intern working on Rhoda Platform, you'll work on the software foundation that keeps our robots running. You'll own real projects on the software platform stack: ranging from on-robot software, networking and communication infrastructure, data collection pipelines, telemetry, teleoperation, inference infra, developer tooling etc., and see your impact run on physical robots by the end of your internship. You'll sit with the engineers who build our robots and ship code that the team depends on every day.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Contribute to the networking and communication infrastructure connecting onboard robot systems to each other, to the cloud, and to teleoperation and monitoring systems

 - Help build data collection pipelines that capture sensor, telemetry, and behavioral data from the robot and upload it reliably to cloud storage for model training

 - Work on telemetry and observability systems that give the team real-time visibility into robot health and field performance

 - Build internal tooling that accelerates robot software development: deployment pipelines, logging, debugging tools, and field testing utilities

 - Support bring-up and field testing on live hardware, debugging issues across the onboard software stack

 - Collaborate with ML, perception, and control engineers to keep onboard systems reliable and training data high quality

 - Automate internal workflows to improve execution efficiency of the Rhoda teams


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field — or a recent graduate

 - Solid computer science foundation: data structures, algorithms, operating systems, and networking

 - Genuine passion for working on robots — coursework, research, personal projects, competition teams, or internships all count

 - Strong programming skills in C++, Python, Golang, or Rust

 - Curiosity and comfort working with physical hardware in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment

 - Ability to debug across layers, from driver-level issues up to application behavior

 - Open to learn new things and grow from knowing nothing to an expert on arbitrary technical topics


NICE TO HAVE (BUT NOT REQUIRED)

 - Experience with bringing up & manipulating robots

 - Familiarity with networking, IPC, or communication protocols (e.g. gRPC, DDS, QUIC, WebSockets)

 - Exposure to cloud storage and data pipelines (AWS, GCP, S3, GCS)

 - Experience with perception pipelines, control systems, or learned models running on real-time robot stacks

 - Prior work on prototype or pre-production hardware


WHY THIS ROLE

 - Your work is the connective tissue of the robot — the networking, data, and tooling infrastructure that determines how fast the team can develop and improve our humanoids in the field

 - Work across the full onboard stack alongside perception, control, and ML engineers & researchers on a platform pushing the frontier of humanoid robotics

 - Real ownership on a small team, with your code running on real robots — not a side project on the shelf

 Job Description: 

 About the Role 
 We are looking for a motivated Software Engineering Intern to work closely with experienced senior developers on a next-generation network management service .
 As an intern, you’ll contribute to a focused engineering project that may involve systems software, automated testing, performance and scale analysis, or developer tooling.
 A key part of the internship will be learning how experienced engineers use AI throughout the software development lifecycle . You’ll use modern AI coding tools to understand existing code, investigate problems, implement changes, troubleshoot failures, generate and improve tests, and analyze results.
 Just as importantly, you’ll learn how to question and validate AI-generated work using tests, measurements, code review, and engineering judgment.
 What You’ll Work On 
 Depending on project priorities, your work could include:
 
• Improving parity and behavioral testing that compares expected behavior across implementations. 
• Testing how network management pipeline components work together, from incoming data through processing to stored or displayed results. 
• Developing end-to-end test scenarios for realistic user, network, or device workflows. 
• Measuring performance and scale and comparing results across configurations or implementations. 
• Improving the tools and automation engineers use to build, test, troubleshoot, and validate software changes. 
• Using AI to understand unfamiliar areas of the codebase, investigate defects, analyze logs and test failures, and propose potential solutions. 
• Participating in code reviews, debugging sessions, and technical discussions with experienced networking software engineers. Working in an AI-Driven Engineering Process 
 This internship is about more than using AI to generate code.
 You’ll learn how experienced developers integrate AI into their engineering workflow:
 Senior developer defines the problem and constraints → Intern works with AI → AI assists with analysis and implementation → Tests and measurements validate the result → Intern reviews the output → Senior developer provides technical guidance 
 You’ll learn how to provide AI with the right technical context, recognize when its suggestions are incomplete or incorrect, and use objective evidence to determine whether a change actually works.
 The goal is to develop both AI fluency and strong engineering judgment .
 Mentorship 
 You’ll work closely with a senior developer who will help:
 
• Define and scope your project. 
• Explain relevant system behavior and architecture. 
• Help you navigate an existing codebase. 
• Guide your use of AI development tools. 
• Review your code, tests, and technical conclusions. 
• Help you understand the engineering trade-offs behind different approaches. You won’t be expected to make product or architecture decisions independently. Instead, you’ll get first-hand experience seeing how experienced engineers approach complex problems and how AI can augment that process .
 What We’re Looking For 
 You may be a good fit if you:
 
• Are pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering , or a related technical field. 
• Have experience programming and debugging software. 
• Understand basic software development concepts such as testing, version control, and code review. 
• Have an interest in networking, systems software, or distributed systems . 
• Are curious about Generative AI, LLMs, and AI-assisted software engineering. 
• Enjoy investigating problems and understanding why something works or fails. 
• Can communicate technical reasoning and findings clearly. 
• Are comfortable questioning and verifying AI-generated suggestions rather than simply accepting them . Experience with Rust, Linux, Git, networking, automated testing, containers, or AI coding tools is helpful, but not required.
 What You’ll Learn 
 During the internship, you’ll gain hands-on experience with:
 
• AI-assisted software engineering. 
• Working directly with senior software developers. 
• Understanding and modifying a production-scale codebase. 
• Network management and systems software. 
• Automated and end-to-end testing. 
• Performance and scale analysis. 
• Debugging and root-cause investigation. 
• Using tests and measurements to validate AI-generated software changes. 
• Professional code review and engineering practices. What Success Looks Like 
 A successful internship will deliver a useful, tested engineering improvement along with a clear explanation of:
 
• What problem was addressed. 
• What changed. 
• How AI was used. 
• How the result was tested and validated. 
• What was learned. 
• What limitations or follow-up work remain. The objective is not simply to generate more code with AI. It is to learn how to use AI effectively and responsibly within a disciplined software engineering process , while developing the technical judgment needed to produce software that engineers can understand, test, and trust.

 Stagiaire en développement de  logiciel, développement assisté par l’IA (Hiver 2027) 

 À propos du poste 
 Nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire en génie logiciel motivé(e) qui travaillera en étroite collaboration avec des développeurs expérimentés sur un service de gestion de réseau de prochaine génération .
 Dans le cadre de ce stage, vous contribuerez à un projet d’ingénierie ciblé pouvant toucher au logiciel système, aux tests automatisés, à l’analyse de la performance et de la mise à l’échelle, ou aux outils destinés aux développeurs.
 Un aspect important du stage consistera à apprendre comment des développeurs expérimentés utilisent l’intelligence artificielle tout au long du cycle de développement logiciel . Vous utiliserez des outils modernes de développement assisté par l’IA pour comprendre du code existant, analyser des problèmes, apporter des modifications, diagnostiquer des défaillances, générer et améliorer des tests et analyser les résultats.
 Tout aussi important, vous apprendrez à remettre en question et à valider le travail généré par l’IA au moyen de tests, de mesures, de revues de code et du jugement d’ingénierie.
 Ce sur quoi vous travaillerez 
 Selon les priorités du projet, vous pourriez notamment :
 
• Améliorer des tests de parité et de comportement afin de comparer les résultats attendus entre différentes implémentations. 
• Tester comment les composants d’une chaîne de traitement de gestion de réseau fonctionnent ensemble, depuis les données d’entrée jusqu’aux résultats stockés ou affichés. 
• Développer des scénarios de test de bout en bout reproduisant des flux de travail réalistes impliquant des utilisateurs, des réseaux ou des équipements. 
• Mesurer la performance et la capacité de mise à l’échelle , et comparer les résultats entre différentes configurations ou implémentations. 
• Améliorer les outils et l’automatisation utilisés par les ingénieurs pour compiler, tester, diagnostiquer et valider les modifications logicielles. 
• Utiliser l’IA pour comprendre des parties moins familières du code, analyser des problèmes, examiner des journaux et des échecs de tests, et proposer des solutions. 
• Participer à des revues de code, des séances de débogage et des discussions techniques avec des ingénieurs expérimentés en logiciels de réseautique. Travailler dans un processus d’ingénierie piloté par l’IA 
 Ce stage va bien au-delà de l’utilisation de l’IA pour simplement générer du code.
 Vous apprendrez comment des développeurs expérimentés intègrent l’IA dans leur processus d’ingénierie :
 Le développeur expérimenté définit le problème et les contraintes → le stagiaire travaille avec l’IA → l’IA contribue à l’analyse et à l’implémentation → les tests et les mesures valident les résultats → le stagiaire examine les résultats → le développeur fournit des conseils techniques 
 Vous apprendrez à fournir à l’IA le contexte technique approprié, à reconnaître lorsque ses suggestions sont incomplètes ou incorrectes et à utiliser des données objectives pour déterminer si une modification fonctionne réellement.
 L’objectif est de développer à la fois votre maîtrise des outils d’IA et votre jugement d’ingénierie .
 Mentorat 
 Vous travaillerez étroitement avec un développeur expérimenté qui vous aidera à :
 
• Définir et délimiter votre projet. 
• Comprendre le comportement et l’architecture du système. 
• Vous familiariser avec une base de code existante. 
• Guider votre utilisation des outils de développement assistés par l’IA. 
• Réviser votre code, vos tests et vos conclusions techniques. 
• Comprendre les compromis techniques associés aux différentes approches. Vous ne serez pas responsable de prendre seul(e) des décisions concernant le produit ou son architecture. Vous aurez plutôt l’occasion d’observer directement comment des ingénieurs expérimentés abordent des problèmes complexes et comment l’IA peut enrichir ce processus .
 Profil recherché 
 Vous pourriez être un excellent candidat ou une excellente candidate si vous :
 
• Poursuivez des études en informatique, génie logiciel, génie informatique ou dans un domaine technique connexe. 
• Possédez une certaine expérience en programmation et en débogage logiciel. 
• Comprenez les principes de base du développement logiciel, notamment les tests, le contrôle de versions et la revue de code. 
• Vous intéressez aux réseaux informatiques, aux logiciels systèmes ou aux systèmes distribués . 
• Êtes curieux ou curieuse au sujet de l’IA générative, des grands modèles de langage (LLM) et du développement logiciel assisté par l’IA. 
• Aimez analyser des problèmes et comprendre pourquoi quelque chose fonctionne ou échoue. 
• Êtes capable de communiquer clairement votre raisonnement et vos conclusions techniques. 
• Êtes à l’aise de remettre en question et de vérifier les suggestions générées par l’IA plutôt que de simplement les accepter . Une expérience avec Rust, Linux, Git, les réseaux informatiques, les tests automatisés, les conteneurs ou les outils de développement assistés par l’IA constitue un atout, mais n’est pas obligatoire.
 Ce que vous apprendrez 
 Au cours du stage, vous développerez une expérience pratique dans les domaines suivants :
 
• Développement logiciel assisté par l’IA. 
• Collaboration directe avec des développeurs expérimentés. 
• Compréhension et modification d’une base de code à grande échelle. 
• Gestion de réseau et logiciels systèmes. 
• Tests automatisés et tests de bout en bout. 
• Analyse de performance et de mise à l’échelle. 
• Débogage et analyse des causes fondamentales. 
• Utilisation de tests et de mesures pour valider les modifications logicielles générées avec l’aide de l’IA. 
• Revues de code et pratiques professionnelles de génie logiciel. À quoi ressemble un stage réussi 
 À la fin du stage, vous aurez livré une amélioration concrète, utile et testée , accompagnée d’une explication claire de :
 
• La problématique abordée. 
• Ce qui a été modifié. 
• La façon dont l’IA a été utilisée. 
• La manière dont les résultats ont été testés et validés. 
• Les principaux apprentissages. 
• Les limites ou travaux complémentaires qui demeurent. L’objectif n’est pas simplement de produire davantage de code grâce à l’IA. Il s’agit d’apprendre à utiliser l’IA de manière efficace et responsable dans le cadre d’un processus rigoureux de génie logiciel , tout en développant le jugement technique nécessaire pour produire des logiciels que les ingénieurs peuvent comprendre, tester et auxquels ils peuvent faire confiance.

 Job Description: 

 About the Role 
 We are looking for a motivated Software Engineering Intern to work closely with experienced senior developers on a next-generation network management service .
 As an intern, you’ll contribute to a focused engineering project that may involve systems software, automated testing, performance and scale analysis, or developer tooling.
 A key part of the internship will be learning how experienced engineers use AI throughout the software development lifecycle . You’ll use modern AI coding tools to understand existing code, investigate problems, implement changes, troubleshoot failures, generate and improve tests, and analyze results.
 Just as importantly, you’ll learn how to question and validate AI-generated work using tests, measurements, code review, and engineering judgment.
 What You’ll Work On 
 Depending on project priorities, your work could include:
 
• Improving parity and behavioral testing that compares expected behavior across implementations. 
• Testing how network management pipeline components work together, from incoming data through processing to stored or displayed results. 
• Developing end-to-end test scenarios for realistic user, network, or device workflows. 
• Measuring performance and scale and comparing results across configurations or implementations. 
• Improving the tools and automation engineers use to build, test, troubleshoot, and validate software changes. 
• Using AI to understand unfamiliar areas of the codebase, investigate defects, analyze logs and test failures, and propose potential solutions. 
• Participating in code reviews, debugging sessions, and technical discussions with experienced networking software engineers. Working in an AI-Driven Engineering Process 
 This internship is about more than using AI to generate code.
 You’ll learn how experienced developers integrate AI into their engineering workflow:
 Senior developer defines the problem and constraints → Intern works with AI → AI assists with analysis and implementation → Tests and measurements validate the result → Intern reviews the output → Senior developer provides technical guidance 
 You’ll learn how to provide AI with the right technical context, recognize when its suggestions are incomplete or incorrect, and use objective evidence to determine whether a change actually works.
 The goal is to develop both AI fluency and strong engineering judgment .
 Mentorship 
 You’ll work closely with a senior developer who will help:
 
• Define and scope your project. 
• Explain relevant system behavior and architecture. 
• Help you navigate an existing codebase. 
• Guide your use of AI development tools. 
• Review your code, tests, and technical conclusions. 
• Help you understand the engineering trade-offs behind different approaches. You won’t be expected to make product or architecture decisions independently. Instead, you’ll get first-hand experience seeing how experienced engineers approach complex problems and how AI can augment that process .
 What We’re Looking For 
 You may be a good fit if you:
 
• Are pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering , or a related technical field. 
• Have experience programming and debugging software. 
• Understand basic software development concepts such as testing, version control, and code review. 
• Have an interest in networking, systems software, or distributed systems . 
• Are curious about Generative AI, LLMs, and AI-assisted software engineering. 
• Enjoy investigating problems and understanding why something works or fails. 
• Can communicate technical reasoning and findings clearly. 
• Are comfortable questioning and verifying AI-generated suggestions rather than simply accepting them . Experience with Rust, Linux, Git, networking, automated testing, containers, or AI coding tools is helpful, but not required.
 What You’ll Learn 
 During the internship, you’ll gain hands-on experience with:
 
• AI-assisted software engineering. 
• Working directly with senior software developers. 
• Understanding and modifying a production-scale codebase. 
• Network management and systems software. 
• Automated and end-to-end testing. 
• Performance and scale analysis. 
• Debugging and root-cause investigation. 
• Using tests and measurements to validate AI-generated software changes. 
• Professional code review and engineering practices. What Success Looks Like 
 A successful internship will deliver a useful, tested engineering improvement along with a clear explanation of:
 
• What problem was addressed. 
• What changed. 
• How AI was used. 
• How the result was tested and validated. 
• What was learned. 
• What limitations or follow-up work remain. The objective is not simply to generate more code with AI. It is to learn how to use AI effectively and responsibly within a disciplined software engineering process , while developing the technical judgment needed to produce software that engineers can understand, test, and trust.

 Stagiaire en développement de  logiciel, développement assisté par l’IA (Hiver 2027) 

 À propos du poste 
 Nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire en génie logiciel motivé(e) qui travaillera en étroite collaboration avec des développeurs expérimentés sur un service de gestion de réseau de prochaine génération .
 Dans le cadre de ce stage, vous contribuerez à un projet d’ingénierie ciblé pouvant toucher au logiciel système, aux tests automatisés, à l’analyse de la performance et de la mise à l’échelle, ou aux outils destinés aux développeurs.
 Un aspect important du stage consistera à apprendre comment des développeurs expérimentés utilisent l’intelligence artificielle tout au long du cycle de développement logiciel . Vous utiliserez des outils modernes de développement assisté par l’IA pour comprendre du code existant, analyser des problèmes, apporter des modifications, diagnostiquer des défaillances, générer et améliorer des tests et analyser les résultats.
 Tout aussi important, vous apprendrez à remettre en question et à valider le travail généré par l’IA au moyen de tests, de mesures, de revues de code et du jugement d’ingénierie.
 Ce sur quoi vous travaillerez 
 Selon les priorités du projet, vous pourriez notamment :
 
• Améliorer des tests de parité et de comportement afin de comparer les résultats attendus entre différentes implémentations. 
• Tester comment les composants d’une chaîne de traitement de gestion de réseau fonctionnent ensemble, depuis les données d’entrée jusqu’aux résultats stockés ou affichés. 
• Développer des scénarios de test de bout en bout reproduisant des flux de travail réalistes impliquant des utilisateurs, des réseaux ou des équipements. 
• Mesurer la performance et la capacité de mise à l’échelle , et comparer les résultats entre différentes configurations ou implémentations. 
• Améliorer les outils et l’automatisation utilisés par les ingénieurs pour compiler, tester, diagnostiquer et valider les modifications logicielles. 
• Utiliser l’IA pour comprendre des parties moins familières du code, analyser des problèmes, examiner des journaux et des échecs de tests, et proposer des solutions. 
• Participer à des revues de code, des séances de débogage et des discussions techniques avec des ingénieurs expérimentés en logiciels de réseautique. Travailler dans un processus d’ingénierie piloté par l’IA 
 Ce stage va bien au-delà de l’utilisation de l’IA pour simplement générer du code.
 Vous apprendrez comment des développeurs expérimentés intègrent l’IA dans leur processus d’ingénierie :
 Le développeur expérimenté définit le problème et les contraintes → le stagiaire travaille avec l’IA → l’IA contribue à l’analyse et à l’implémentation → les tests et les mesures valident les résultats → le stagiaire examine les résultats → le développeur fournit des conseils techniques 
 Vous apprendrez à fournir à l’IA le contexte technique approprié, à reconnaître lorsque ses suggestions sont incomplètes ou incorrectes et à utiliser des données objectives pour déterminer si une modification fonctionne réellement.
 L’objectif est de développer à la fois votre maîtrise des outils d’IA et votre jugement d’ingénierie .
 Mentorat 
 Vous travaillerez étroitement avec un développeur expérimenté qui vous aidera à :
 
• Définir et délimiter votre projet. 
• Comprendre le comportement et l’architecture du système. 
• Vous familiariser avec une base de code existante. 
• Guider votre utilisation des outils de développement assistés par l’IA. 
• Réviser votre code, vos tests et vos conclusions techniques. 
• Comprendre les compromis techniques associés aux différentes approches. Vous ne serez pas responsable de prendre seul(e) des décisions concernant le produit ou son architecture. Vous aurez plutôt l’occasion d’observer directement comment des ingénieurs expérimentés abordent des problèmes complexes et comment l’IA peut enrichir ce processus .
 Profil recherché 
 Vous pourriez être un excellent candidat ou une excellente candidate si vous :
 
• Poursuivez des études en informatique, génie logiciel, génie informatique ou dans un domaine technique connexe. 
• Possédez une certaine expérience en programmation et en débogage logiciel. 
• Comprenez les principes de base du développement logiciel, notamment les tests, le contrôle de versions et la revue de code. 
• Vous intéressez aux réseaux informatiques, aux logiciels systèmes ou aux systèmes distribués . 
• Êtes curieux ou curieuse au sujet de l’IA générative, des grands modèles de langage (LLM) et du développement logiciel assisté par l’IA. 
• Aimez analyser des problèmes et comprendre pourquoi quelque chose fonctionne ou échoue. 
• Êtes capable de communiquer clairement votre raisonnement et vos conclusions techniques. 
• Êtes à l’aise de remettre en question et de vérifier les suggestions générées par l’IA plutôt que de simplement les accepter . Une expérience avec Rust, Linux, Git, les réseaux informatiques, les tests automatisés, les conteneurs ou les outils de développement assistés par l’IA constitue un atout, mais n’est pas obligatoire.
 Ce que vous apprendrez 
 Au cours du stage, vous développerez une expérience pratique dans les domaines suivants :
 
• Développement logiciel assisté par l’IA. 
• Collaboration directe avec des développeurs expérimentés. 
• Compréhension et modification d’une base de code à grande échelle. 
• Gestion de réseau et logiciels systèmes. 
• Tests automatisés et tests de bout en bout. 
• Analyse de performance et de mise à l’échelle. 
• Débogage et analyse des causes fondamentales. 
• Utilisation de tests et de mesures pour valider les modifications logicielles générées avec l’aide de l’IA. 
• Revues de code et pratiques professionnelles de génie logiciel. À quoi ressemble un stage réussi 
 À la fin du stage, vous aurez livré une amélioration concrète, utile et testée , accompagnée d’une explication claire de :
 
• La problématique abordée. 
• Ce qui a été modifié. 
• La façon dont l’IA a été utilisée. 
• La manière dont les résultats ont été testés et validés. 
• Les principaux apprentissages. 
• Les limites ou travaux complémentaires qui demeurent. L’objectif n’est pas simplement de produire davantage de code grâce à l’IA. Il s’agit d’apprendre à utiliser l’IA de manière efficace et responsable dans le cadre d’un processus rigoureux de génie logiciel , tout en développant le jugement technique nécessaire pour produire des logiciels que les ingénieurs peuvent comprendre, tester et auxquels ils peuvent faire confiance.

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. The Front End Platform team is looking for a Developer Intern to join a cross-functional group of developers and designers. Our main goal is to help teams achieve higher efficiency, consistency, and scalability when building 1Password products. 

Our areas of focus are:

 - Establishing frontend foundational standards and tooling across our codebases

 - Creating and maintaining a library of reusable design components and usage guidelines



This is a remote opportunity within Canada or the US. This position will be for 4 months - January to April 2027.



What you can expect:

 - Assist our team in building React components from Figma specifications.

 - Implement coded components in our customer-facing applications.

 - Leverage an understanding of software development practices at 1Password to help define standards and best practices for developing frontend code.

 - Develop and utilize tooling to streamline the design and development process for new features.

 - Collaborate with people from across many countries, disciplines and experience levels, who all care a lot about what we’re building.
   
   

What we're looking for:

 - Confidence: A willingness to take on new challenges, and see them through to completion.

 - Humility: You're not afraid to ask "stupid" questions and make mistakes (as long as you learn from them).

 - Curiosity: You look for better ways of doing things, even if everyone seems happy with how they are.

 - Teamwork: We work together, and succeed as a team!



Bonus points for:

 - Experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, and/or React.

 - Familiarity with accessibility standards and inclusive design practices.

 - Experience with Git, SSH, 1Password Command Line Tool, CI/CD pipelines and/or cloud providers.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of most roles. Frequency will depend on role and responsibilities, and may include, but is not limited to: annual department-wide offsites, team meetings, and customer/industry events. 


How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

Job Description 
 Kickstart Your Career at Vertex!   
Are you ready to make a real impact? At Vertex, our mission is to tackle serious diseases and to change lives, for the better, for the future. Our aim is to give you the skills, insights, and career guidance to be an important part of that future; to turn your potential into progression. As a Vertex intern or co-op, you’ll work on meaningful projects, collaborate with talented teams, and learn from industry leaders. We’re passionate about innovation, inclusion, and supporting your growth—inside and outside the lab. 
  
 Why Vertex?  
 
• Real Projects:  You’ll work on assignments that make a real impact, not just busy work.  
• Mentorship & Networking:  Connect with leaders and peers who want to see you succeed through professional networks, connections, and collaborations that will shape your longer-term career.  
• Flexible & Supportive:  We offer flexible work options with Flex @ Vertex and prioritize your wellbeing.  
• Inclusive Culture:  Collaboration and inclusion are embedded in everything we do.  
• Career Launchpad:  Build skills, explore career paths, and get guidance for your future career.   
 Your Impact  
 The Vertex Human-AI Work and Organization Design Co-Op is a 6-month experiential training program for students currently working towards an advanced degree in Organizational Design, Organizational Behavior, Industrial-organizational Psychology, Human-Computer Interaction, Strategy, Management, Operations, Sociology, Anthropology, Organizational Sociology, Learning Sciences, Organizational Learning, Systems Design, Service Design, Process Design, Information Systems, Data Science, or other related fields focused on Human-AI interaction. If you are passionate, collaborative, and growth-minded, a co-op at Vertex will help you gain meaningful experience in our Workforce Strategy & Innovation functional areas and serve as a launchpad for your career.  
  
 The application deadline for this co-op is November 15th. Please note that Vertex reviews applications on a rolling basis and reserves the right to close this job posting prior to the listed deadline. Applicants can expect to receive an update about their application before or shortly after the application deadline.   
  
 Ready to apply? Submit your application and let’s turn possibilities into reality!  
  
   What you will be doing:   
Vertex is advancing an enterprise AI transformation that will evolve how work is performed, how teams operate, and how Vertexians collaborate with AI agents to deliver value. Human-AI Design is a major component of our transformation, and involves analyzing work at the task level, designing future-state human-AI processes, and translating those processes into roles, team structures, workforce plans, and organization designs.
  
 The Graduate Co-op, Human-AI Work and Organization Design will report to the Senior Director of Human-AI Process Design and work closely with Human-AI Design Leads and other stakeholders within HR and beyond to capture lessons from active transformation work, synthesize insights across initiatives, and translate emerging experience into improved methodologies, tools and standards.
  
 The co-op will also conduct research on human-AI collaboration, the future of work, AI-enabled organization design, team evolution, organizational learning, and measurement. By connecting external research with evidence from Vertex’s transformation initiatives, the co-op will help Vertex develop a rigorous and practical approach to redesigning work for an AI-enabled future.
  
 This role is well suited for a graduate or doctoral student interested in conducting applied research at the intersection of Future of Work, artificial intelligence, work design, organization design, and enterprise transformation.
  
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Capture and synthesize lessons from Vertex’s AI Transformation

• Partner with Human-AI Design Leads working across transformation pods to document design decisions, methods used, challenges encountered, and lessons learned. 
• Review outputs from pod-level work, including future-state processes, task and work inventories, role definitions, team structures, organization designs, and workforce impact analyses. 
• Identify recurring patterns, differences, and unresolved questions across transformation initiatives. 
• Distinguish broadly transferable practices from approaches that are specific to a particular function, process, or business context. 
• Translate pod-level experience into concise case studies, research summaries, design guidance, and recommendations for methodology improvements.  
 Evolve Vertex’s Human-AI design methodology
 
• Help refine the methodology used by Human-AI Design Leads to analyze work at the task level and identify opportunities to automate, augment, simplify, or reallocate work. 
• Support the development of frameworks for determining which activities should be performed by people, AI agents, or a combination of both. 
• Help improve methods for translating future-state processes into role definitions, team structures, decision rights, workforce implications, and organization designs. 
• Identify gaps in the methodology based on evidence from active transformation work and relevant external research. 
• Support the continued development of Vertex’s playbook for executing end-to-end human-AI work transformations.  
 Advance Organization Design for the AI era
 
• Research how AI-enabled work may affect roles, team composition, organizational structures, coordination mechanisms, and spans of responsibility. 
• Explore how teams may evolve when people work alongside AI assistants and autonomous or semi-autonomous agents. 
• Help adapt established organization design principles and tools for work environments in which AI performs a meaningful share of tasks.  
 Research measurement in the age of AI
 
• Research emerging approaches for measuring the impact of AI-enabled work and organization redesign. 
• Help distinguish measures of AI deployment or usage from measures of sustainable business and organizational impact and identify potential qualitative and quantitative methods for evaluating human-AI workflows and transformation outcomes. 
• Work with Human-AI Design Leads to identify measures that can be applied consistently across pods while accounting for differences in business context.  
 Facilitate organizational learning and knowledge transfer
 
• Research effective approaches for transferring learning among groups participating in Vertex’s AI transformation. 
• Help establish a recurring process through which Human-AI Design Leads share methods, findings, challenges, and reusable solutions. 
• Support workshops, retrospectives, working sessions, and communities of practice focused on human-AI work design. 
• Prepare cross-pod learning summaries, presentations, research briefs, and playbook updates. 
• Surface emerging questions that require additional research, experimentation, or leadership decisions. 
• Help shorten the learning cycle between pod-level experimentation and enterprise-level methodology improvement.  
 Collaborate across the transformation
 
• Build productive working relationships with Human-AI Design Leads and selected partners across business functions, HR, technology, data, transformation, change, and learning. 
• Participate in selected pod working sessions to observe how human-AI design methods are applied in practice. 
• Conduct interviews, working sessions, artifact reviews, and structured retrospectives to capture knowledge. 
• Facilitate organizational learning and knowledge transfer  
 Qualifications: 
 
• Currently pursuing a master’s degree, doctoral degree, or equivalent graduate-level program in a relevant field, such as: 
• Organization design or organizational behavior. 
• Industrial-organizational psychology. 
• Human-computer interaction. 
• Management, strategy, or operations. 
• Sociology, anthropology, or organizational sociology. 
• Learning sciences or organizational learning. 
• Systems design, service design, or process design. 
• Information systems, data science, or another interdisciplinary field focused on human-AI interaction. 
• Strong interest in the future of work, artificial intelligence, human-AI collaboration, organization design, and/or workforce transformation. 
• Demonstrated ability to conduct structured research and synthesize findings from academic research, practitioner experience, interviews, and work products. 
• Experience in using AI tools to evolve own ways of working (e.g., reviewing/synthesizing information, developing deliverables, automating tasks) 
• Strong conceptual and systems-thinking skills, including the ability to connect task, process, role, team, workforce, and organization-level implications. 
• Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills. 
• Ability to translate complex information into practical frameworks, tools, playbook content, and executive-ready materials. 
• Ability to work effectively in an environment where methods, technologies, and organizational requirements continue to evolve. 
• Ability to manage defined work independently while collaborating with experienced practitioners and cross-functional partners. 
• Legal authorization to work in the United States, now and in the future. Please note that Vertex does not provide sponsorship for internships/co-ops or entry level roles within this part of the organization.  
• You must be enrolled in an advanced degree program if graduating before May 2027  
• You must be available to work full-time, 40 hours per week from January – July 2027   
 Program Details:    
 
• Full-time, paid co-op $30.00 – 50.00 USD/hour  
• Program Dates: January – July 2027  
• Application Deadline: November 15th, 2026
